<reason>PRO won on enforceability and necessity. B answered both CON pressures directly with an outcome-anchored trigger and a traces test for real judgment, turning rubber-stamp and gate fears into arguments for the right. CON's broad-equals-collapse charge was embraced as caseload-is-lives, while CON's audit-plus-targeted-appeal still let the model choose who gets a human and its algorithm-can-give-reasons reply missed liability and ownership. Clipped opening added execution cost to CON.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The B4.1-A1 outcome trigger plus B4.3-A2 traces test answered A3.1-A3.2 more cleanly than A4.1-A4.2 answered B3.1-B3.2, letting B close the gate and make audit without a human look like the machine grading its homework.</best_rebuttal>
